userStories.title: Approval releases a redeem request without executing it
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make explicit and timeout approval release redeem requests into a bounded approved state without executing their commands.

**Motivation** — The 11 routes left on `PENDING_GATE_ROUTES` take or return a secret.

**Approach** — `ApprovalExecutionService.execute` is the one choke point for approve paths. Five callers execute a request after approving it (the decide route, `ApprovalDecisionService.decide`, `ApprovalRouteCommands`' deferred decision, the fleet `ApprovalsService` and `FleetApprovalRouteCommands`), plus the sweeper. `execute` answers a redeem request unchanged, after its `approved` check, and runs nothing. None of those callers changes. The decide route therefore answers the request with status `approved`.

The approve step (`ApprovalDecisionService.recordDecision`, the `approved` transition patch), and the sweeper's timeout approve (`ApprovalRequestExpirySweeper.settleOne`):
```ts
// Redeem requests restart their clock at approval: the window is the request's own ask timeout.
const redeemWindow = request.redeem === true ? { expiresAt: new Date(now.getTime() + (request.expiresAt.getTime() - request.createdAt.getTime())) } : {};
```
The default ask timeout is `DEFAULT_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_SEC` (86,400 s), so a request opened under a policy with no `timeoutSec` can be redeemed for 24 hours after approval.

`findStaleApproved` gains `redeem: false` in its `where`. Preserve the existing decidedAt cutoff, ordering and limit. Do not run precheck or parse stored input for redeem execution; its stored input may omit required secret fields. Only the approved transition of a redeem request gains expiresAt: non-redeem approvals and rejection patches retain their current shape. Pending onTimeout:'approve' still records its existing timeout attribution and calls execute after commit; execute is now a no-op for redeem. Preserve ordinary non-redeem execution and every caller's public return type.

**Scope** — In: execute no-op, explicit approval/timeout window reset and stale retry exclusion, using existing execution/decision/sweeper unit specs and repository integration cases. Out: selecting and expiring approved redeem rows (US-003), requester redemption and raw-result return (US-004), route/header contracts and pilots (US-005/006/007). A configurable redeem window, or a policy field for it: the window is the request's own ask timeout (ruling 2026-10-29).

**Interface** — `ApprovalExecutionService.execute(requestId: string, now: Date = new Date()): Promise<ApprovalRequestRecord>` remains unchanged; redeem is an early return only after existence and approved-status checks.

Verification: extend approval-execution.service.spec.ts, approval-decision.service.spec.ts, approval-request-expiry.sweeper.spec.ts and approval-repositories.integration.spec.ts without changing existing non-redeem fixtures. Strict three-session TDD; real-DB stale selection verification outside the sandbox.

userStories.title: The sweeper expires unredeemed approvals
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expire approved redeem requests that were not redeemed before their restarted deadline, preserving fleet timeout ownership and concurrent-settlement safety.

**Motivation** — Gating them like the others would leak it.

**Approach** — The sweeper's due scan (`PrismaApprovalRequestRepository.findDue`) widens its status condition. The two fleet `NOT EXISTS` clauses stay:
```sql
WHERE (r."status" = 'pending' OR (r."status" = 'approved' AND r."redeem")) AND r."expiresAt" <= ${now}
```
`settleOne` takes a locked `approved` redeem row past its `expiresAt` to `expired`, regardless of its `onTimeout` (the `onTimeout: 'approve'` branch applies only to `pending` rows), (`transition(id, 'approved', { status: 'expired', settledAt: now })`). It records its event and the audit entry `system.approval.expire` with summary `redeem expired <permissionKey>`. It calls no `canSettleTimeout`, because a redeem request has no fleet link. `findStaleApproved` gains `redeem: false` in its `where`.

US-002 already owns the stale-approved exclusion and pending timeout-approval clock reset; preserve those. Re-read status and deadline under the existing per-request lock: a row now executed is ignored, and a later expiresAt is no longer due. Keep ordinary pending timeout behavior, row-order/limit and both fleet exclusions unchanged. An approved redeem expiration is counted as expired, never as a new timeout approval, and never calls execution.execute. Events and audit remain in the settlement transaction; a failed compare-and-set must not emit a phantom settlement.

**Scope** — In: findDue SQL and approved-redeem settlement/event/audit behavior with unit and repository integration assertions. Out: approving/resetting deadlines (US-002), redemption (US-004), route pilots (US-006/007). Cancelling an approved, unredeemed request: it expires on its own (ruling 2026-10-29); `POST /approvals/:id/cancel` keeps refusing a non-pending request.

**Interface** — `findDue(now: Date, limit: number): Promise<ApprovalRequestRecord[]>` and `tick(now = new Date()): Promise<ApprovalRequestExpiryResult>` retain their signatures. `tick` reports `{ expired, approved, failed }` using the existing counters.

Verification: extend approval-request-expiry.sweeper.spec.ts and approval-repositories.integration.spec.ts, using existing approval-expiry.integration.spec.ts as context if needed; preserve fleet regression assertions. Each expiry/event/audit AC is its own isolated fixture. Strict three-session TDD and DB verification outside the sandbox.

userStories.title: The redeem flag in the request DTO and the documented header
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose the redeem flag consistently in approval summary/detail responses and document the optional redemption header on redeem-gated handlers.

**Motivation** — `GET /api/approvals/:id` shows both to the requester and to every principal who may decide the request.

**Approach** — The approval id header is read with Nest's `@Headers(APPROVAL_REDEEM_HEADER)`. `APPROVAL_REDEEM_HEADER = 'x-koda-approval-request'` (lower case, as Fastify and Express present header names). There is no format check: an unknown value reads as a missing request (404). An empty value is treated as absent: `ApprovalRouteGate.run` takes the redeem branch only for a non-empty `redeem`.

`@ApprovalGated({ redeem: true })` documents the header with `@ApiHeader({ name: 'X-Koda-Approval-Request', required: false, description })`. `@ApprovalGated()` with no options is unchanged.

Declare `redeem` on `ApprovalRequestFields` (so both the summary and the detail DTO document it), mapped in `ApprovalRequestSummaryDto.from`. Map `record.redeem === true` to an explicit Boolean: absent domain flags become false in HTTP responses. Detail uses the stored redacted input, never reconstructs the original body. Preserve the summary's exact allowlist and date/null serialization; its existing expected object gains redeem:false. The redeem decorator option must retain APPROVAL_GATED_METADATA:true, ApprovalPendingFilter, JsonResponse envelope and the documented 202 response; without the option it adds no header metadata.

US-005 and US-006 change the documented API (the `redeem` field, the 202s and the header), but `openapi.json` is regenerated once, in US-007: the OpenAPI contract specs read the committed file, so regenerating earlier would break their 115-operation case before US-007 updates it.

**Scope** — In: DTO mapping/Swagger field, exported header constant and decorator option, plus approval-http.spec.ts and decorator unit assertions. Out: route-gate redemption/error behavior (US-004), adding handler header parameters and pilot commands (US-006/007), regenerated OpenAPI/count updates (US-007). Validating the header's format: an unknown or malformed value reads as a missing request.

**Interface** —
```ts
APPROVAL_REDEEM_HEADER = 'x-koda-approval-request'
ApprovalGated(options?: { redeem?: boolean })
```
`ApprovalRequestSummaryDto.redeem: boolean` is declared through the shared fields class.

Verification: DTO AC-1 through AC-3 live in approval-http.spec.ts; extend approval-gated.decorator.spec.ts for AC-4 through AC-7 while preserving existing metadata assertions. Add a database-free Nest probe handler there for the non-ApprovalPending error regression: ValidationAppException must keep its normal 400 response instead of reaching the pending filter. Do not boot the full database-backed application for this decorator unit case. Use strict three-session TDD for the secret-approval public contract.

userStories.title: Gated agent create and key rotation, redeemed by the requester
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Gate agent creation and key rotation with redeem commands so approved requesters receive one-time API keys directly and the approval row stores no API key.

**Motivation** — So `POST /admin/users` under a wait policy would store the temporary password in plain JSON, and `POST /agents` would store the new API key.

**Approach** — Agent cache eviction moves after commit. `AgentsService.generateApiKey` evicts the agent's auth cache (`invalidateByTag`) inline today, on both create and rotate. Inside a deferred execution, that eviction would run before the commit, and a concurrent auth read could re-cache the old key hash for one TTL. Both branches use the existing `invalidateAfterCommit(agentId)`. With no scope open, it runs at once, as today.

The rotate route reads its target first, as 5c-2's `agent.delete` does: `findBySlug(slug)` before the gate (404 `agents` as today), and the input carries `{ slug, agentId }`. The command rotates `agentId`, so a slug reused after the request opened is not rotated.

Each pilot story removes its own rows from `PENDING_GATE_ROUTES` and `SECRET_GATE_ROUTES`. US-006 sets the exact counts to its own state (117 gated routes, 9 allowlist rows); US-007 sets them to 118 and 8.

The handlers keep their `@Requires`, `@HttpCode`, `@Throttle` and `@ApiResponse`s, gain `@ApprovalGated({ redeem: true })` and an `@Headers(APPROVAL_REDEEM_HEADER) redeem?: string` parameter (last), and have this shape:
```ts
const outcome = await this.routeGate.run<{ apiKey: string; agent: AgentResponseDto }>({
  key: 'agent.create', variant: AGENT_ROUTE_VARIANTS.create, projectId: null, input: { agent: createAgentDto }, redeem,
});
if (outcome.status === 'pending') throw new ApprovalPending(outcome.request);
return JsonResponse.Ok(outcome.result);
```
`AgentsController`'s public test seams `createAgent` and `rotateKey` stay as they are; the HTTP handlers stop calling them, as `update` and `remove` stopped calling theirs in 5c-2.

Register the two variants in existing AgentRouteCommands.onModuleInit using routeCommand. `POST /agents` uses key `agent.create`, global project null, variant `rest:agents.create`, input `{ agent: parseBody(CreateAgentDto, …) }`, no redact (stored whole), run `agents.generateApiKey(input.agent)`, `toResult: ({ agent }) => ({ agent })`. `POST /agents/:slug/rotate-key` uses key `agent.key.rotate`, global project null, variant `rest:agents.rotate-key`, input `{ slug, agentId }` (target read first), no redact, run `agents.generateApiKey(input.agentId)`, `toResult: ({ agent }) => ({ agent })`. Both declare redeem:{}; raw apiKey is only returned to the executing HTTP caller. Preserve canonical DTO validation, slug collision errors, normal no-policy behavior and human bypass under any wait policy.

Update agent-route.commands.spec.ts, agents.service.spec.ts and agents.controller.spec.ts for registrations, after-commit eviction and gate call arguments; keep direct test-seam cases unchanged. In agents-create.routes.spec.ts and agent-create-canonical-dto.routes.spec.ts, the ApprovalRouteGate double's run answers `{ status: 'executed', result: await <the testing module's AgentsService>.generateApiKey(call.input.agent) }` for agent.create so existing HTTP assertions retain actual service behavior. Remove only these two routes from both secret/pending lists. Update the explicit-list/assignment unit assertions to nine remaining gate-secret routes and booted-app count to exactly 117, adjusting their titles. Do not regenerate openapi.json until US-007.

**Scope** — In: two agent variants, HTTP handlers, cache timing, intermediate contract counts and the new gated-agent-key-routes.integration.spec.ts. Out: admin user create/hash preparation and final 118/8/OpenAPI contract (US-007); engine/DTO/header changes are upstream. `AgentsController`'s public test seams `createAgent` and `rotateKey`: they keep calling the service directly. Moving `recordAgentAction` after commit: it writes nothing without a project id, and these routes pass none.

**Interface** — `AGENT_ROUTE_VARIANTS.create = 'rest:agents.create'`; `AGENT_ROUTE_VARIANTS.rotateKey = 'rest:agents.rotate-key'`. Existing overloads:
```ts
async generateApiKey(agentId: string): Promise<{ apiKey: string; agent: AgentResponseDto }>;
async generateApiKey(dto: CreateAgentDto): Promise<{ apiKey: string; agent: AgentResponseDto }>;
```
HTTP handler parameter order is generateApiKey(dto, principal, redeem?) and rotateApiKey(slug, principal, redeem?).

Verification: the requesting agent holds only global agent.create and agent.key.rotate, followed by PermissionCache.invalidate(). Mirror gated-agent-routes.integration.spec.ts, seed a wait policy per test, approve through the real root-authenticated decisions route and redeem by repeating the same HTTP call with X-Koda-Approval-Request. Reset throttle and delete policy/decision/request rows before each test; each AC recreates its complete lifecycle with unique slugs. Compare localized error text using the file-local approvals message helper, restore spies in afterEach and close the app. Strict three-session TDD; run the real DB/HTTP cases outside the sandbox.

userStories.title: Gated admin user create with the password redacted, and the contract counts
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Gate admin user creation with password-redacted redemption and out-of-transaction hashing, then finalize the three-route 118-gated/8-pending OpenAPI and permission contract.

**Motivation** — So `POST /admin/users` under a wait policy would store the temporary password in plain JSON, and `POST /agents` would store the new API key.

**Approach** — The admin user create hashes outside the transaction. `UsersAdminService.prepareCreate(dto)` (new) normalises the email, refuses a taken one (409 `users`) and runs `bcrypt.hash`. It answers a callback that writes the user, its baseline binding and the audit entry. `create(dto)` becomes `(await this.prepareCreate(dto))()`. The command's `prepare` uses `prepareCreate`, so bcrypt (cost 12) never runs inside the execution transaction. The callback keeps today's unique-violation catch (409 `users`), so a concurrent create of the same email is still refused.

Each pilot story removes its own rows from `PENDING_GATE_ROUTES` and `SECRET_GATE_ROUTES`. US-006 sets the exact counts to its own state (117 gated routes, 9 allowlist rows); US-007 sets them to 118 and 8.

The raw password never enters ApprovalRequest.input, ApprovalRequest.inputHash, ApprovalRequest.result or any audit summary; the normal User.passwordHash is still persisted by the mutation callback. Redemption parses the full resent body; the password can change because only email/name are bound into the stored hash. Keep all existing DTO/password constraints, lower-case trimmed email normalization, member baseline and safe user result DTO. Immediate execution uses create, which performs the same preparation itself. Preserve the atomic user/baseline/audit writes and after-commit behavior inside the returned mutation callback.

The handlers keep their `@Requires`, `@HttpCode`, `@Throttle` and `@ApiResponse`s, gain `@ApprovalGated({ redeem: true })` and an `@Headers(APPROVAL_REDEEM_HEADER) redeem?: string` parameter (last).
